title: Take-Two Boss 'Not in the Least' Concerned Bad Press Will Affect GTA 6 Launch
description: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has stated he is unconcerned that negative press surrounding Rockstar's employment tribunal will impact GTA 6.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Take-Two CEO Addresses Controversy Surrounding Rockstar Games

In recent news reported by Eurogamer, Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick has addressed concerns regarding the recent negative press and employment tribunal involving Rockstar Games. When asked about the potential fallout, Zelnick stated that he is "not in the least" concerned that these controversies will affect the upcoming launch of Grand Theft Auto 6.

### The Context of the Controversy

As one of the most anticipated entertainment releases in history, GTA 6 has been under intense public and media scrutiny. Recently, developer Rockstar Games has faced negative press concerning alleged union-busting and related employment tribunal issues. In the gaming industry, labor disputes and public scrutiny are matters that occasionally draw significant attention from both media outlets and players.

While some observers might wonder if such PR challenges could create headwinds for the game, Take-Two's leadership has made it clear they do not expect it to dent the momentum of their flagship franchise.

### Industry Perspective on Major AAA Launches

Industry analysts often note that titles with the sheer cultural and economic footprint of the GTA series possess a unique resilience against external controversies. Historical precedents in the gaming sector show that massive consumer demand and long-standing player anticipation frequently outweigh short-term media controversies when a blockbuster finally hits the market.

By dismissing the potential impact so plainly, Zelnick reinforces the company's unwavering confidence in the drawing power of Rockstar's upcoming title.

## Editor's Take

Zelnick's confidence underscores the sheer, unshakeable market dominance of the GTA franchise. While commercial success for a titan like GTA 6 seems all but guaranteed regardless of PR turbulence, the situation highlights the growing importance of corporate responsibility and labor relations in modern game development.
